patch.name: SafetyChain
securityEvidenceBlockers: SafetyChain's documented Record Data Extract access-token endpoint requires grant_type=password; the WFM connector plane forbids OAuth resource-owner password grants.

SafetyChain documents that Access to Integration API Scope can view all records and resources; WFM forbids broad cross-scope reads unless a narrower effective scope or customer-controlled constrained projection is proven.
patch.evidenceNote: SafetyChain's current Developer Hub documents Record Data Extract, Supplier Onboarding and Process APIs. Read-oriented endpoints include locations, resources, forms, records, requirements and tasks, and several read operations are transported as POST with Take/Skip/PageSize pagination, so HTTP verb alone cannot determine mutation authority. The same API family also exposes mutative form, resource, record, task, supplier-document and workflow operations; those remain outside WFM authority. SafetyChain states that bearer tokens are environment-bound and its RDE token endpoint currently requires the password grant. Its Integration API Scope is documented as able to view all records and resources. WFM therefore reuses the existing REST adapter only for an explicit route allowlist of verified read/extract operations, keeps writes and cross-scope reads disabled, and blocks evidence promotion to authenticated stages until a vendor-supported non-password least-privilege identity or a customer-controlled constrained read projection is proven. Plant-floor connectivity described by SafetyChain is not inherited as PLC/SCADA authority by this cloud/application connector.

requiredPermissions: dedicated SafetyChain integration identity or customer-controlled read projection restricted to the approved tenant, sites, locations, resources and record families
explicit allowlist of documented read/extract operations only; POST transport does not by itself confer mutation authority
no form/resource/record/task creation, supplier-document approval, hold release, corrective-action mutation or other process write authority
no plant-floor, PLC, MES-control or equipment-write authority inherited from SafetyChain's broader integration capabilities

a vendor-supported authentication route that does not require the resource-owner password grant, or a customer-controlled facade that terminates that legacy credential outside WFM and exposes a separately authenticated constrained read API
dataAvailableOrExpected: locations and location hierarchy plus customer-defined location attributes
resources such as equipment, items, suppliers and related customer-defined attributes
forms, form definitions, quality checks, audits and record data intentionally exposed through the integration APIs
tasks, requirement status, supplier/compliance records and corrective-action context where the licensed API/module exposes them
production and process-quality observations recorded in SafetyChain, including out-of-spec and hold/corrective-action context
user references and audit/change context tied to API activity where exposed
automationOpportunities: use current quality/hold/non-conformance state to warn planners when production demand is constrained or additional QA labour is likely to be required
join controlled quality and training evidence to customer-defined schedule-readiness checks without treating a SafetyChain record as automatic legal work eligibility
use supplier/certification and receiving-quality status to anticipate inspection workload and receiving labour demand
reuse location, resource and form metadata during implementation to reduce manual site/resource mapping and duplicate administration
correlate paid labour, overtime and skills mix with quality records, scrap/rework and production outcomes for finance and executive reporting
after separate write certification only, consider narrowly scoped task or workflow hand-offs without granting generic Process API mutation authority
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time and avoidable overtime by exposing quality holds, out-of-spec conditions and inspection workload to labour planning sooner
reduce duplicate quality/compliance administration by reusing governed SafetyChain locations, resources, forms and record evidence
reduce rework and quality-loss cost by correlating recurring quality outcomes with staffing level, skill mix and shift conditions
reduce receiving and supplier-compliance administration by reusing supplier requirement/certification status where licensed and safely scoped

the publicly documented RDE authentication path uses a password grant and therefore cannot currently satisfy the normal WFM connector authentication policy
the documented Integration API Scope can see all records and resources, so least-privilege site/entity scope is not proven by the role name alone
public documentation does not establish one universal rate-limit contract across every API family; per-endpoint throttling and retry behaviour require authorised validation
customer-defined forms, resources, attributes and location structures require schema fingerprints and deterministic mapping versioning
quality/training evidence does not automatically establish legal qualification or work eligibility

tokens are environment-bound and Live/Train or other environments must be pinned independently rather than reusing credentials or assuming identical data/configuration

Before any sandbox or tenant authentication, obtain vendor confirmation of a non-password least-privilege authentication option with narrower effective record/resource scope, or deploy a customer-controlled constrained read projection that terminates the legacy/broad credential outside WFM. Then prove effective site/entity scope, enumerate the licensed read endpoints, validate rate limits/retry/token-refresh behaviour, normalise representative location/resource/quality/compliance records and only promote evidence after an authorised read round-trip.

patch.name: AspenTech Inmation OT Data Fabric
patch.evidenceNote: AspenTech documents Inmation as an industrial data fabric spanning cloud, edge and on-premises estates with OPC/OPC UA, ODBC, files, MQTT, Kafka, HTTP, Modbus and other OT/IT connectivity plus store-and-forward buffering for intermittent networks. Its Web API documentation exposes controlled read endpoints for current values, quality/timestamps, model hierarchy, files and historical data. Authentication supports Profile Credentials or Windows accounts with Basic or bearer-token modes. Endpoint permissions explicitly separate READ/LIST from WRITE/MODIFY and executable-function surfaces. No Inmation sandbox or tenant authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: dedicated customer-authorised profile limited to READ and only the minimum LIST access required for model/path discovery
site/model scope restricted to approved industrial objects and histories
read current values, quality, timestamps, hierarchy and historical data only where required
customer-edge termination for OPC UA, MQTT, Modbus and other plant-network protocols
explicit denial of WRITE, MODIFY, upload, batch-update, execfunction and process/control operations
dataAvailableOrExpected: current industrial values with source quality and timestamps
hierarchical asset/model and connector/core/parent/system paths
raw and processed historical telemetry
industrial events/signals exposed through the customer model
files and metadata stored in authorised file stores
batch production records where a customer model exposes the documented read surface
context from legacy and modern upstream sources including OPC, PI/PHD, MQTT, Kafka, ODBC and files
automationOpportunities: use current and historical machine/production state to refresh staffing requirements and downtime redeployment recommendations
coordinate maintenance windows and skill demand from industrial state without direct cloud scanning of plant networks
reuse an existing customer OT data fabric to connect legacy plants and reduce separate point-to-point OT integrations
preserve source quality and event time so low-quality or delayed telemetry cannot silently drive live staffing automation
resume buffered site ingestion after outages using per-site watermarks and deterministic dedupe
correlate cross-site production and labour outcomes for forecasting and executive reporting
savingsHypotheses: reduce connector engineering by reusing the customer's governed industrial data fabric
reduce paid idle labour through earlier trustworthy downtime/recovery signals
reduce emergency maintenance overtime through better operational-state coordination
reduce data-loss reconciliation effort at intermittently connected sites through store-and-forward aware ingestion
reduce manual cross-system reporting by retaining source lineage and canonical industrial mappings

constraintsRisks: store-and-forward can replay old data after connectivity returns; delayed telemetry must never be mistaken for current machine state
Basic or Windows-integrated authentication requires deployment-specific hardening; bearer/profile credentials are preferred when they can be scoped safely
large historical reads require bounded time windows, checkpoints and backpressure
duplicate observations can enter through multiple upstream collectors and must be deduplicated with source lineage intact
the Web API exposes WRITE, MODIFY and executable-function capabilities; the WFM credential must be technically prevented from reaching them
edge and plant protocols require a customer-controlled gateway and no direct cloud plant-network access
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST, OPC UA, MQTT, Kafka, database, file and Modbus profiles rather than building new transports. Add a thin Inmation Web API adapter that discovers only authorised model paths, enforces READ/LIST-only operation allowlists, preserves value/quality/source timestamp, reads bounded history, tracks per-site watermarks, deduplicates buffered replay, fingerprints customer model mappings and records source lineage. Keep all plant protocols at the customer edge and prohibit WRITE/MODIFY/execfunction routes. Then obtain an authorised test profile for sandbox/tenant authentication and a read round-trip.

patch.evidenceNote: Current HighByte documentation confirms a REST Data Server, MQTT, OPC UA, role/claim-based access control and API keys. Claims distinguish read/list/execute-read from execute-write/publish and can scope selected resources by tags. The same product also exposes API-trigger pipelines, MCP tools and i3X surfaces that can execute writes/configuration. Manufacturing WFM therefore uses only explicitly allowlisted read/list/execute-read data paths behind the customer edge. API-trigger pipelines, MCP tools, i3X write-capable paths, configuration APIs and central-management operations remain excluded until separately authorised and evidenced. No HighByte instance was authenticated or queried.

tag-scoped resource claims where available so the connector cannot browse unrelated factory/site content
HTTPS plus customer-approved certificate trust; MQTT subscribe-only and OPC UA Browse/Read/Subscribe only with named authenticated sessions where those transports are used
no execute-write, publish, create, update, delete, pipeline action, MCP configuration/action, central-hub administration or project import/export authority
dataAvailableOrExpected: modelled industrial instances and namespace hierarchy representing sites, lines, assets and processes
raw or contextualised operational values from connected OT/IT sources through REST Data Server reads
MQTT/Sparkplug-style telemetry and OPC UA values/events when customers expose approved read-only projections
connection/model/instance metadata needed to map source tags and hierarchy into canonical WFM objects
historical or calculated values where the customer's configured source and model expose them, marked with transformation provenance

adjust staffing and redeployment recommendations from actual line/machine availability without direct PLC access
correlate labour cost, downtime, throughput and energy through one governed OT projection
use common REST/MQTT/OPC UA abstractions across factories whose underlying PLC, historian, SQL or MES technologies differ
accelerate diagnostics through connection/model metadata without granting project or management-plane authority

reduce paid idle time by matching labour recommendations to actual equipment availability
reduce overtime caused by delayed visibility of production recovery or line constraints
reduce implementation mapping effort by reusing model, instance and namespace hierarchy
improve labour-to-output and labour-to-energy attribution without expanding control authority

Discover version/capabilities read-only, verify dedicated claims contain no execute-write/publish/configuration actions, bind allowed models/instances/tags to a customer/site mapping, preserve source/event and ingestion time plus raw-versus-derived provenance, and keep API-trigger pipelines, MCP, i3X writes and central-management APIs disabled until separately authorised. Obtain an authorised lab/customer instance before promotion beyond spec verification.

patch.evidenceNote: Microsoft documents Business Central API v2.0 over REST/OData, cloud environment and company scoping, OAuth/S2S access, server-driven paging, throttling/recovery guidance and webhook subscriptions. Online APIs are enabled by default; on-premises endpoints are customer-managed and APIs must be enabled by an administrator. No sandbox or tenant authentication was performed, so this promotion is specification evidence only.
securityEvidenceBlockers: Service-to-service access requires an Entra application permission named API.ReadWrite.All even for a read-only WFM integration. Before authentication evidence advances, prove a dedicated Business Central application identity with narrowly assigned Business Central permission sets and effective denied mutations; the Entra scope name itself is not proof of read authority.

Business Central resource APIs can expose POST, PATCH, DELETE and business actions as well as GET. Steady-state WFM must use executor-enforced exact read-route and method allowlists; successful bearer authentication is not evidence of least privilege.

On-premises Business Central endpoints are customer-managed and may sit behind private networks/firewalls. WFM must use an authorised customer-edge/TLS route and never directly scan or bridge the private network; legacy Basic/access-key authentication must not be preferred when an approved OAuth/S2S deployment is available.

The Business Central application contains manufacturing data such as production orders, BOMs, routings, work centres and machine centres, but standard API v2 documentation does not establish complete standard endpoints for those objects. WFM must not infer API availability from application functionality; manufacturing enrichment requires a separately verified custom API, published OData/query, analytics/export or middleware route.

Webhook subscription creation and three-day renewal are mutating control-plane operations. Normal read-only runtime cannot silently acquire that authority; use customer-controlled provisioning/renewal or continue polling and reconciliation.

narrow Business Central application permission sets for required read objects; do not assign SUPER and prove mutations are denied
pin api.businesscentral.dynamics.com for cloud or an explicitly approved customer-edge endpoint for on-premises; prohibit arbitrary hosts and redirects
scope every read and checkpoint by connection plus tenant/environment/company for cloud, or serverInstance/company for on-premises
if webhooks are used, separate customer-approved subscription creation/renewal authority from steady-state read credentials and bind clientState to the expected source scope

patch.evidenceNote: Intelex's current developer documentation verifies a REST/JSON API over each customer's configured application model. V2 supports Basic and API-key authentication; the newer V6 secure API supports client-credentials bearer tokens when enabled. API requests preserve platform security settings for the effective user, but API-key and secure-token setup is limited to Admin/Full Access users, so authenticated evidence must prove the resulting technical identity is actually constrained to the approved records. The API is tenant/custom-object driven rather than a fixed EHS schema, caps sequential result pages at 500 records with @odata.nextLink paging, and documents a platform rate limit of 6 requests per second with 429/Retry-After semantics. WFM therefore reuses the existing REST adapter with customer-model discovery, explicit field/object allowlists, bounded paging and adaptive backoff; mutative object/user/task operations remain outside normal connector authority.

read-only access to the specific EHS/QMS/training/reference objects needed by WFM; no record creation, workflow action, task reassignment, user provisioning or archive/revoke authority
HTTPS with tenant hostname pinned; no arbitrary instance URLs or cross-host redirects

patch.evidenceNote: Epicor provider documentation establishes versioned, discoverable, OData v4-compliant REST services across Kinetic business objects, processes, reports, BAQs and Epicor Functions, with API keys/access scopes/standard authentication methods and security aligned to ERP user/data permissions. Provider documentation also establishes cloud, on-premises and hybrid Kinetic deployment choices. No sandbox or customer tenant was authenticated and no live read round-trip was performed, so this is specification evidence only.

providerIdentity.regionalHostModel: provider-managed cloud region or customer-managed on-prem/hybrid instance; endpoint is deployment-specific

governedReadProjection.note: Epicor documents BAQs as reusable governed data views exposed through REST. Prefer a reviewed BAQ/read projection for WFM extraction when it narrows data and authority versus full business-object/process/function services.

Full service parity therefore includes mutating and executable surfaces; WFM must prove exact read-only service/projection authority and keep processes/functions/actions outside steady-state runtime authority.

Public provider material reviewed establishes API keys, access scopes and standard authentication methods but does not prove the exact customer deployment flow, effective scopes, rotation/revocation behaviour or denied writes. Advance authentication evidence only in an authorised sandbox/tenant with a dedicated least-privilege identity.

BAQs and user-defined fields can expose customer-specific schemas. Exact projection ids, parameters, fields, company/site scope and stable identifiers must be reviewed, fingerprinted and fail closed on breaking drift.

Public provider material reviewed does not establish one universal pagination, delta-token, rate-limit or webhook completeness contract for every Kinetic deployment/service. Discover those contracts from the authorised tenant REST help/metadata and keep bounded polling/reconciliation authoritative until proven.
On-premises/private Kinetic deployments require an authorised customer-edge route. WFM must not scan, bridge or directly expose customer private networks.

Epicor Functions execute custom server-side logic and are excluded from the default connector authority even though they are REST-accessible. Enabling any function/action/write path requires separate explicit approval and proof.
